bills.title: Artificial Intelligence Transparency and Accountability Act
bills.summary: This bill establishes disclosure and reporting requirements for certain organizations that deploy artificial intelligence systems. It requires covered entities to notify users when they interact with AI, maintain documentation of high-risk systems, conduct impact assessments before deployment, and submit annual transparency reports to the state. The measure also directs the Attorney General to publish guidance and receive complaints related to noncompliance, while creating limited exemptions for research and small businesses.
bills.officialSummary: An act to add Division 3.5 to the Civil Code, relating to artificial intelligence, requiring disclosure, documentation, impact assessment, and reporting by covered deployers of automated decision systems, and authorizing enforcement by the Attorney General.

actions.action: Introduced in Senate. Read first time.
Referred to Assembly Privacy and Consumer Protection.
Approved by the Governor. Chaptered by Secretary of State.

editorial.policyGoal: Improve transparency and accountability in the use of artificial intelligence systems that affect Californians.
editorial.problemAddressed: Consumers and constituents may not know when they are interacting with an AI system or when automated systems influence important decisions about services, benefits, or opportunities.
editorial.policyMechanism: Mandatory disclosure, documentation, impact assessments, and annual reporting requirements for covered AI deployers, with Attorney General oversight.
appliesTo: Private companies deploying covered AI systems in California
Developers of high-risk AI systems offered to California deployers
State agencies using automated decision tools
requirements: Notify users when they are interacting with AI
Maintain documentation about covered AI systems
Conduct impact or risk assessments before deployment
Provide information to the responsible state agency
Establish an appeal or review process for adverse automated decisions

implementation.rulemakingAuthority: Department of Technology, in consultation with the Attorney General
implementation.funding: General Fund appropriation for first-year implementation support

enforcement: Attorney General may bring civil actions for violations
Administrative remedies available for incomplete reporting
No private right of action under this chapter
Penalties may include injunctive relief and civil fines for willful noncompliance
exemptions: Small businesses below a statutory revenue threshold
Accredited research institutions conducting non-commercial research
Certain public safety systems as defined by regulation
Federally regulated entities to the extent of conflict with federal law

keyProvisions.title: AI Disclosure Requirements
keyProvisions.description: Covered organizations must notify users when they are interacting with certain artificial intelligence systems in customer-facing or consequential decision contexts.

keyProvisions.title: Impact Assessments
keyProvisions.description: Deployers of high-risk AI systems must evaluate reasonably foreseeable risks before deployment and retain assessment records for audit.

keyProvisions.title: Annual Reporting
keyProvisions.description: Covered entities must submit regular reports describing the use, oversight, and known incidents involving AI systems.

keyProvisions.title: Appeal Pathways
keyProvisions.description: Individuals subject to adverse automated determinations must be offered a meaningful human review process.

bills.title: State AI Procurement Standards Act
bills.summary: Establishes minimum transparency, bias-testing, and vendor documentation requirements for artificial intelligence systems purchased by state agencies. Directs the Department of Information Technology to issue model contract clauses within one year of enactment.

editorial.policyMechanism: Statutory requirements and agency oversight for covered AI uses.

bills.title: Facial Recognition Moratorium in Public Spaces
bills.summary: Prohibits municipal and state law enforcement from using real-time facial recognition in publicly accessible areas, with limited exceptions for court-authorized investigations. Creates a private right of action for unlawful use.

bills.title: Automated Decision Systems Fairness Act
bills.summary: Mandates pre-deployment fairness audits for automated systems used in public benefits eligibility, hiring for state employment, and housing assistance determinations. Requires agencies to offer human review upon request.

bills.title: Generative AI Use in State Communications Act
bills.summary: Requires disclosure when generative artificial intelligence is used to produce official state publications, press materials, or public-facing digital content. Directs agencies to retain human editorial oversight for all generative outputs.

bills.title: Data Privacy and Artificial Intelligence Safeguards Act
bills.summary: Limits the use of personally identifiable data in training and operating government AI systems. Requires data minimization plans and breach notification timelines specific to AI-processed datasets.

bills.title: Public Sector Algorithm Inventory Act
bills.summary: Directs each executive agency to inventory algorithms and machine learning models used in service delivery and report annually to the legislature. Creates a centralized state algorithm catalog accessible to the public.

bills.title: AI Vendor Risk Assessment Requirements
bills.summary: Requires state procurement officers to complete standardized AI risk assessments before awarding contracts for machine learning or generative AI products. Prohibits sole-source awards for high-risk AI systems without legislative notification.

bills.title: Biometric Surveillance Oversight Act
bills.summary: Creates a statewide biometric surveillance oversight board and requires warrants for law enforcement use of facial recognition matching against civilian databases. Establishes annual reporting on query volume and accuracy rates.

bills.title: Automated Eligibility Determinations Review Act
bills.summary: Requires human review of adverse automated eligibility decisions for Medicaid, SNAP, and unemployment insurance within ten business days. Mandates plain-language notices explaining the role of automated systems.

bills.title: Generative AI Workforce Training Pilot Program
bills.summary: Authorizes a three-year pilot program to train state employees on responsible use of generative AI tools for drafting, summarization, and constituent correspondence. Requires evaluation of productivity and error rates before statewide expansion.

bills.title: AI Training Data Provenance Disclosure Act
bills.summary: Requires vendors supplying AI systems to state agencies to disclose categories of training data, known data provenance gaps, and any use of copyrighted or personally identifiable material. Applies to contracts executed after January 1, 2027.

bills.title: Municipal Algorithmic Impact Assessment Mandate
bills.summary: Requires cities with populations over 100,000 to complete algorithmic impact assessments before deploying automated systems that affect housing, policing, or social services. Provides matching grants for compliance assistance.

bills.title: State Cloud AI Services Contracting Act
bills.summary: Establishes preferred contracting frameworks for cloud-hosted AI services, including audit rights, data residency requirements, and termination-for-bias provisions. Directs the Chief Information Officer to publish a model RFP within 180 days.

bills.title: School Campus Facial Recognition Restrictions
bills.summary: Bars public K-12 schools and community colleges from installing facial recognition systems without parental notice and school board approval. Exempts one-time event security under narrowly defined emergency conditions.

bills.title: Automated Sentencing Advisory Tool Ban
bills.summary: Prohibits courts from relying on proprietary automated risk assessment tools for sentencing recommendations unless the methodology and training data are disclosed to defense counsel. Creates a judicial technology advisory panel.

bills.title: Generative AI Legislative Drafting Guardrails Act
bills.summary: Authorizes limited use of generative AI to assist legislative staff with bill drafting and research summaries, subject to mandatory human authorship attestation. Prohibits using generative AI to fabricate citations or statutory cross-references.

bills.title: Consumer AI Profiling Opt-Out Act
bills.summary: Grants residents the right to opt out of automated profiling by businesses that sell or share AI-derived consumer scores with state agencies. Requires agencies to honor opt-out requests within 30 days.

bills.title: Independent AI Audit Authority Act
bills.summary: Creates an Independent AI Audit Authority empowered to compel production of model documentation from agencies and vendors. Authorizes public summary reports while protecting trade secrets under a sealed-review process.

bills.title: AI Systems Accessibility and Language Equity Act
bills.summary: Requires AI-enabled public service interfaces to meet accessibility standards and provide equivalent service quality in the state's most commonly spoken non-English languages. Directs agencies to test disparate error rates across language groups.

bills.title: Statewide AI Procurement Preference Program
bills.summary: Creates a preference for AI vendors that publish open evaluation benchmarks and commit to independent bias testing. Caps preference points and requires annual legislative reporting on award outcomes.

bills.title: Transit Hub Facial Matching Prohibition
bills.summary: Prohibits transit authorities from deploying facial matching technology for passenger screening or fare enforcement. Allows limited use for investigating violent felonies with judicial authorization.

bills.title: Agency Generative AI Content Labeling Act
bills.summary: Requires clear labeling of images, audio, and video generated or substantially altered by generative AI when published by state agencies. Establishes civil penalties for knowing failure to disclose synthetic media.

bills.title: Sensitive Data Ban for Public AI Models
bills.summary: Prohibits state agencies from uploading health, tax, or juvenile justice records into third-party generative AI platforms. Requires agency-approved enterprise tools with contractual data-retention limits.

bills.title: High-Risk Automated System Registry Act
bills.summary: Defines high-risk automated decision systems and requires registration with the state Attorney General before deployment. Authorizes the Attorney General to seek injunctive relief for unregistered high-risk systems.

bills.title: Public Benefits Chatbot Standards Act
bills.summary: Sets accuracy, escalation, and nondiscrimination standards for generative AI chatbots used to assist residents with public benefits applications. Requires quarterly accuracy audits and public posting of error rates.

bills.title: Automated Hiring Tool Disclosure for State Contractors
bills.summary: Requires companies contracting with the state to disclose use of automated hiring tools and provide adverse-action notices when such tools contribute to rejection of applicants for contract-related positions.

bills.title: AI Model Lifecycle Documentation Act
bills.summary: Requires agencies to maintain lifecycle documentation for AI models, including intended use, update history, known failure modes, and retirement criteria. Makes documentation available to legislative oversight committees upon request.

bills.title: Law Enforcement AI Tool Procurement Moratorium
bills.summary: Imposes a two-year moratorium on new procurement of predictive policing and facial recognition tools by law enforcement pending completion of a statewide civil liberties review. Allows renewal of existing contracts under current terms only.

bills.title: Cross-Border Data Transfer Limits for State AI
bills.summary: Restricts transfer of state-held personal data to foreign jurisdictions for AI training or inference without a documented risk assessment and Attorney General approval. Applies to vendors processing data on behalf of agencies.

bills.title: Statewide Strategic Performance Planning Act
bills.summary: Requires executive agencies to adopt four-year strategic plans aligned with statewide priority outcomes and publish annual progress dashboards. Directs the Governor's Office of Planning to issue guidance and templates.

keyProvisions.description: Requires executive agencies to adopt four-year strategic plans aligned with statewide priority outcomes and publish annual progress dashboards. Directs the Governor's Office of Planning to issue guidance and templates.

bills.title: Interagency Coordination and Priority Setting Act
bills.summary: Creates a cabinet-level Priority Coordination Council to align cross-agency initiatives and reduce duplicative planning mandates. Requires biennial reports identifying overlapping programs and consolidation opportunities.

bills.title: Long-Range Capital Investment Planning Act
bills.summary: Mandates a ten-year statewide capital investment plan integrating transportation, water, and broadband priorities. Requires public hearings in each region before plan adoption.

bills.title: Community-Informed Strategic Planning Requirements
bills.summary: Requires agencies developing strategic plans to conduct structured community engagement and document how public input influenced final priorities. Establishes minimum accessibility standards for planning materials.

bills.title: Climate Resilience Strategic Framework Act
bills.summary: Directs the state to adopt a climate resilience strategic framework with measurable adaptation goals for coastal, agricultural, and urban areas. Requires agency plans to incorporate framework targets by 2028.

bills.title: Workforce Development Strategic Alignment Act
bills.summary: Aligns workforce board strategic plans with projected labor-market demand and regional economic development strategies. Requires annual updates using common labor-market indicators.

bills.title: Statewide Performance Measures Standardization Act
bills.summary: Establishes a common set of core performance measures for major public services and requires agencies to report against them in budget documents. Creates a technical working group to refine measure definitions.

bills.title: Results-Based Budgeting Performance Act
bills.summary: Ties a portion of discretionary agency funding to demonstrated progress on legislatively approved performance targets. Requires mid-cycle corrective action plans when targets are missed by more than 15 percent.

bills.title: Public Dashboard Transparency for Agency Performance
bills.summary: Requires each cabinet agency to maintain a publicly accessible performance dashboard updated at least quarterly. Mandates machine-readable data exports for independent analysis.

bills.title: Equity-Centered Performance Metrics Act
bills.summary: Requires agencies to disaggregate key performance measures by race, ethnicity, geography, and disability status where statistically feasible. Directs the state demographer to publish methodological guidance.

bills.title: Local Government Performance Benchmarking Act
bills.summary: Creates a voluntary statewide benchmarking program for municipal service performance and authorizes technical assistance grants. Prohibits use of benchmarking data alone as grounds for funding reductions.

bills.title: Customer Experience Performance Standards Act
bills.summary: Establishes customer-experience performance standards for high-volume citizen services such as licensing and tax assistance. Requires agencies to publish wait-time and resolution-rate metrics monthly.

bills.title: Independent Outcome Evaluation Mandate Act
bills.summary: Requires major new spending programs above a defined threshold to commission independent outcome evaluations within three years of launch. Establishes a roster of prequalified evaluation vendors.

bills.title: Evidence-Based Policy Review Act
bills.summary: Creates an Evidence Review Office to assess whether proposed and existing programs are supported by credible outcome evidence. Requires legislative fiscal notes to cite available evaluation findings.

bills.title: Randomized Evaluation Pilot Authorization
bills.summary: Authorizes agencies to conduct randomized controlled evaluations of selected social service interventions with ethics board oversight and informed consent where required. Directs publication of evaluation protocols before enrollment begins.

bills.title: Tax Credit Outcome Reporting Act
bills.summary: Requires recipients of major economic development tax credits to report employment and wage outcomes using standardized metrics. Authorizes clawbacks when committed outcomes are not achieved within the agreement period.

bills.title: Education Program Outcome Transparency Act
bills.summary: Requires state-funded education interventions to publish outcome evaluations covering student achievement, completion, and equity gaps. Creates a searchable repository of evaluation reports.

bills.title: Housing Assistance Impact Evaluation Act
bills.summary: Directs the housing finance agency to evaluate the impact of rental assistance and homelessness prevention programs on housing stability and employment. Requires a report to the legislature every two years.

bills.title: Criminal Justice Diversion Outcome Study Act
bills.summary: Funds a multi-year outcome study of pretrial diversion and reentry programs, measuring recidivism, employment, and treatment engagement. Requires comparison groups and open data practices where legally permissible.

bills.title: Health Program Cost-Effectiveness Evaluation Act
bills.summary: Requires periodic cost-effectiveness evaluations of major Medicaid pilot programs and chronic disease initiatives. Directs findings to inform reauthorization decisions and public reporting.
